rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.title: Rate of Change of Momentum for a Particle
rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.description: This equation states that the time rate of change of a particle's momentum is equal to the net external force acting on it.
rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.conceptual_definition: This equation is a fundamental statement of classical mechanics, often referred to as Newton's Second Law in its momentum form. It quantifies how the motion of an individual particle changes due to external influences. The net external force causes a change in the particle's momentum over time, directly linking force to the dynamics of motion.
rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.interpretation: The left side, $\dot{\mathbf{p}}_i$, represents the instantaneous rate at which the momentum vector of particle $i$ is changing, which can involve changes in magnitude, direction, or both. The right side, $\mathbf{F}_{i, ext{net}}$, is the vector sum of all external forces acting *only* on particle $i$. This equation establishes a direct causal link: forces cause changes in momentum. If the net external force on a particle is zero, its momentum remains constant, which is a statement of Newton's First Law for that particle.
rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.limits_and_boundary: This equation is valid within the domain of classical mechanics, applying to particles moving at speeds significantly less than the speed of light ($v \ll c$) and at scales much larger than quantum mechanical effects. It assumes the mass of the particle remains constant over time. Its application is typically within an inertial reference frame.
rate-of-change-of-momentum-for-a-particl.symmetry_origin: While this equation describes how momentum changes, its integral form (the impulse-momentum theorem) is closely related to the conservation of momentum. The conservation of total momentum for a system of particles arises from summing this equation over all particles and applying Newton's Third Law for internal forces, which itself is linked to the translational symmetry of space.

deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.title: Deceleration Parameter in a Radiation-Dominated Universe
deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.description: Relates the cosmological deceleration parameter $q$ directly to the radiation density parameter $\Omega_r$ in a cosmos dominated by relativistic fluid or radiation.
deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.conceptual_definition: In standard Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology, the deceleration parameter $q = -\frac{\ddot{a} a}{\dot{a}^2}$ quantifies the rate of cosmic expansion deceleration. For a relativistic fluid characterized by the equation-of-state parameter $w = 1/3$, the second Friedmann acceleration equation yields $q = \frac{1+3w}{2}\Omega_r = \Omega_r$ in the absence of other matter components or cosmological constant terms.
deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.interpretation: The parameter $q$ represents the dimensionless cosmic deceleration rate. The quantity $\Omega_r \equiv \frac{\rho_r}{\rho_c}$ is the fractional energy density of relativistic species relative to the critical density $\rho_c = \frac{3H^2}{8\pi G}$. When the energy density is entirely comprised of radiation ($\\Omega_r = 1$ in a flat universe), the universe experiences a deceleration parameter of $q = 1$, corresponding to a scale factor growth of $a(t) \propto t^{1/2}$.
deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.limits_and_boundary: In the limit of a spatially flat, pure radiation epoch ($\Omega_r \to 1$), $q \to 1$. As the universe expands and transitions toward matter dominance ($z \ll z_{\text{eq}}$), $\Omega_r \to 0$ and $q$ relaxes to $\frac{1}{2}\Omega_m$.
deceleration-parameter-in-radiation-domi.symmetry_origin: Derived from the Einstein field equations assuming spatial homogeneity and isotropy (FLRW metric) under the continuous $SO(3)$ rotational and translational isometry groups.

infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.title: Infinite Yukawa Coupling Limit
infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.description: Represents the asymptotic regime where the dimensionless Yukawa coupling constant $y_f$ diverges towards infinity, signifying non-perturbative strong coupling between a fermion species and the scalar Higgs sector.
infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.conceptual_definition: The infinite Yukawa coupling limit $y_f \to \infty$ formally characterizes the strong-coupling regime of scalar-fermion Yukawa interactions $y_f \bar{\psi}_L \Phi \psi_R + \text{h.c.}$. In the electroweak symmetry-broken phase with a finite vacuum expectation value $\langle \Phi \rangle = v / \sqrt{2}$, this limit formally sends the tree-level fermion mass $m_f = y_f v / \sqrt{2} \to \infty$, decoupling the fermion from the low-energy effective field theory while inducing a severe Landau pole and violating perturbative unitarity at high energies.
infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.interpretation: In this asymptotic limit, the dimensionless parameter $y_f$ approaches $\infty$. Given the relation $m_f = y_f v / \sqrt{2}$, where $v \approx 246\text{ GeV}$ is the electroweak vacuum expectation value, diverging $y_f$ implies $m_f \to \infty$. Perturbative expansion in powers of $y_f^2 / (4\pi)$ becomes invalid, the perturbative partial-wave unitarity bound (typically $y_f \lesssim \sqrt{8\pi/3}$) is violated, and the corresponding fermion can be integrated out of the low-energy effective Lagrangian as a heavy frozen degree of freedom.
infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.limits_and_boundary: In the opposite limit $y_f \to 0$, the fermion decouples from the scalar vacuum and chiral symmetry is restored in the massless limit $m_f \to 0$. In the limit $y_f \to \infty$, a non-perturbative regime is entered, with an ultraviolet Landau pole emerging at finite energy scales $\Lambda \sim v \exp(8\pi^2 / (3 y_f^2))$.
infinite-yukawa-coupling-limit-3ea6a689.symmetry_origin: Chiral symmetry $U(1)_L \times U(1)_R$ of the fermion is explicitly broken by the Yukawa coupling to the scalar sector down to the vector subgroup $U(1)_V$.

orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.title: Orthogonality of Four-Velocity and Four-Acceleration
orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.description: Expresses the geometric orthogonality between a massive particle's four-velocity and four-acceleration in Minkowski spacetime, arising directly from the constancy of the four-velocity magnitude.
orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.conceptual_definition: For any massive particle moving along a timelike worldline parameterized by proper time $\tau$, the four-velocity $U^\mu$ satisfies the invariant pseudo-norm constraint $U_\mu U^\mu = -c^2$ (or $-1$ in natural units). Differentiating this invariant scalar condition with respect to $\tau$ yields $\frac{d}{d\tau}(U_\mu U^\mu) = 2 U_\mu \frac{dU^\mu}{d\tau} = 0$. This confirms that the four-acceleration vector $A^\mu = \frac{dU^\mu}{d\tau}$ is strictly orthogonal to the four-velocity $U^\mu$ in the four-dimensional Minkowski metric.
orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.interpretation: The factor of $2$ originates from applying the product rule to the quadratic scalar invariant $U_\mu U^\mu$. The index $\mu \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ denotes the spacetime indices contracted using the metric tensor $\eta_{\mu\nu}$. The vector $U_\mu$ represents the covariant four-velocity, and $\frac{dU^\mu}{d\tau}$ is the contravariant four-acceleration with respect to the particle's invariant proper time $\tau$. The vanishing contraction $2 U_\mu \frac{dU^\mu}{d\tau} = 0$ proves that four-acceleration has no longitudinal component along the worldline tangent vector.
orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.limits_and_boundary: In the non-relativistic limit $v \ll c$, the temporal component of the identity yields the classical work-energy relation $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\right) = \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{v}$, resolving the apparent spatial non-orthogonality of $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{a}$. For massless particles ($v = c$), proper time $\tau$ is degenerate ($d\tau = 0$), requiring affine parameterization along null geodesics.
orthogonality-of-4-velocity-and-4-accele.symmetry_origin: Rooted in Lorentz group $SO(1,3)$ invariance and the metric compatibility of flat Minkowski spacetime (or curved pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, where $\nabla_\sigma g_{\mu\nu} = 0$).
